## Definitions

- [statement] Classic multi-planner winner is the plan that produces the most results during the trial while doing the least work; the winning multi-planner score is reported in explain executionStats-era fields, distinct from CBR costEstimate. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/core/query-plans/ · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, explain plan, Cost-Based Ranker and Multi-Planning Changes (8.3 and 9.0)
- [passage] - If `$lookup` is the last stage or all stages after `$lookup` can be executed using the slot-based execution engine, the `queryPlanner` object is in the top-level `explain` output object (`explain.queryPlanner`). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#lookup-optimization · keywords: $lookup, queryPlanner, explain, explain.queryPlanner

## Structure and components

- [statement] Planning time (optimizationTimeMillis) excludes time spent optimizing inner $lookup queries. Since 8.0 rejectedPlans contain only the find portion; earlier versions could include aggregation stages such as $group. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: aggregation explain, explain plan, spill statistics, Aggregation Explain and Spill Statistics ($lookup and $group and memory limits)
- [passage] | Field | Description | Applicable Stages | | --- | --- | --- | | `docsExamined` | Specifies the number of documents scanned during the query execution stage. | `COLLSCAN`, `FETCH` | | `keysExamined` | For query execution stages that scan an index `keysExamined` is the total number of in-bounds and out-of-bounds keys that are examined in the process of the index scan. If the index scan consists of a single contiguous range of keys, only in-bounds keys need to be examined. If the index bounds consists of several key ranges, the index scan execution process may examine out-of-bounds keys in order to skip from the end of one range to the beginning of the next. | `IXSCAN` | | `numReads` | The number of documents scanned or index keys examined during the query execution stage. **New in version 5.1** | `COLLSCAN`, `IXSCAN` | | `seeks` | The number of times that we had to seek the index cursor to a new position in order to complete the index scan. | `IXSCAN` | | `usedDisk` | Whether the stage wrote to disk. **New in version 5.3** | `GROUP` | | `spills` | The number of times the stage spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledBytes` | The total amount of data written to disk in bytes. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledRecords` | The total number of individual records spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledDataStorageSize` | The total disk space, in bytes, used by the spilled data. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `peakTrackedMemBytes` | **New in version 8.3** Maximum number of bytes of tracked memory in use by the current query operation. Starting in MongoDB 9.0, the `COUNT_SCAN`, `GEO_NEAR_2D`, `GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE`, and `UPDATE` stages also report this field. | `COUNT_SCAN`, `GEO_NEAR_2D`, `GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE`, `GROUP`, `SORT`, `UPDATE` | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, explain plan, spill statistics, docsExamined, COLLSCAN, FETCH
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, when you run `explain` in a mimumum of [executionStats](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#std-label-explain-method-executionStats) verbosity mode, aggregation stages that use the classic query execution engine output a `expressionEvaluationPeakMemoryBytes` field. This field contains the peak memory usage, in bytes, from expression evaluation during stage execution. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#aggregation-stages-with-expression-memory-tracking · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, explain plan, spill statistics, explain, expressionEvaluationPeakMemoryBytes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [statement] The explain field mergeType reports where the merger part runs; the documented examples show mongos and anyShard. Search summaries of the docs also list specificShard (with a mergeShard field naming the shard) and router, but the page text for those was not directly verified. — https://www.practical-mongodb-aggregations.com/guides/sharding.html · keywords: explain plan, sharded explain, Sharded Explain and Split Pipelines (SHARD_MERGE and per-shard stats and merge shard selection)
- [passage] If you run [`explain`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/explain.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.explain) on a `$setWindowsFields` operation, the output contains a `peakTrackedMemBytes` field that contains the maximum number of bytes of tracked memory in use. For more information, see [`explain.executionStats.peakTrackedMemBytes`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats.peakTrackedMemBytes) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/setWindowFields.md#explain-output · keywords: explain plan, spill statistics, explain, $setWindowsFields, peakTrackedMemBytes, explain.executionStats.peakTrackedMemBytes
- [passage] When you downgrade the FCV from `9.0` to an earlier version, a migration updates the stored query settings. The migration removes every knob whose minimum FCV exceeds the target version and deletes any settings entry that still contains only default values. Re-upgrading to `9.0` does not restore the removed knobs. You must re-apply them with `setQuerySettings`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, 9.0, setQuerySettings
- [passage] The second case occurs when the merge part of the split pipeline contains a stage which may write temporary data to disk, such as $group, and the client has specified allowDiskUse:true. In this case, assuming that there are no other stages in the merge pipeline which require the primary shard, the merge runs on a randomly-selected shard in the set of shards targeted by the aggregation. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: mongodb-advanced-explain-and-planner-changes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md
- [fact] The random-shard merge exists so the merger part has more disk space available for spilling blocking stages when allowDiskUse is true; with allowDiskUse false, streaming-only mergers stay on mongos. — https://www.practical-mongodb-aggregations.com/guides/sharding.html · keywords: Sharded Explain and Split Pipelines (SHARD_MERGE and per-shard stats and merge shard selection)
- [passage] The first case occurs when the merge part of the split pipeline contains a stage which *must* run on a specific shard. For instance, if `$lookup` requires access to an unsharded collection in the same database as the sharded collection on which the aggregation is running, the merge runs on the shard that hosts the unsharded collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md#routing-and-results-process · keywords: $lookup · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/
- [passage] Contains partial execution information captured during the plan selection phase for both the winning and rejected plans. The field is present only if explain runs in allPlansExecution verbosity mode. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: mongodb-advanced-explain-and-planner-changes
- [passage] Object that contains two fields: true and false. Each field counts the number of matching queries where the value of usedDisk is true or false, respectively. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: spill statistics
- [passage] When splitting the aggregation pipeline into two parts, the pipeline is split to ensure that the shards perform as many stages as possible with consideration for optimization. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-sharded-collections.md#optimization · keywords: mongodb-advanced-explain-and-planner-changes
- [passage] Contains metrics related to CBR when it is used during query planning. CBR evaluates multiple query plans and selects the most efficient plan based on estimated costs. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: cost-based ranker
- [passage] Contains metrics related to the number of documents sampled during cost-based ranking for queries with the given key. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: cost-based ranker
- [passage] Contains counts for each cardinality estimation method used during cost-based ranking. Each field represents the number of times a particular estimation method was used. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: cost-based ranker
- [passage] mergeType shows where the stage of the merge happens ("anyShard", "specificShard", or "router"). When mergeType is specificShard, the aggregate output includes a mergeShard property that contains the shard ID of the merging shard. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: sharded explain · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md
- [passage] If the query optimizer uses the cost-based ranker, the output contains several additional fields. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: cost-based ranker

## How it works

- [statement] CVE-2026-4358 (published 2026-03-17): a crafted $lookup aggregation by an authenticated user with write privileges can trigger a double-free or use-after-free in the SBE engine when an in-memory hash table is spilled to disk. CVSS v4 6.1 medium, v3 7.5. — https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-4358 · keywords: aggregation explain, explain plan, spill statistics, Aggregation Explain and Spill Statistics ($lookup and $group and memory limits)
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.3, multi-planning with a CBR backup is the default plan selection mechanism for eligible queries. For a short trial period, the multi-planner attempts to find a plan capable of returning a result set within this short timeframe. If the attempt is unsuccessful, MongoDB applies a set of rules to determine whether the multi-planner should continue or if CBR should evaluate each node in the plan to determine the optimal plan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#queryplanner · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, explain plan · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/core/query-plans/
- [fact] Explain output for CBR plans adds costEstimate, cardinalityEstimate, numKeysEstimate, numDocsEstimate and estimatesMetadata.ceSource per stage, marked new in 8.3.3. ceSource values: sampling, heuristics (only when sampling fails), mixed, metadata, code. A large gap between numKeysEstimate and costEstimate can indicate a problem with the winning plan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, explain plan, Cost-Based Ranker and Multi-Planning Changes (8.3 and 9.0)
- [statement] Percona lists reduced multi-planning cost among 8.3 performance improvements and says the new serverStatus counters and explain output show when CBR was used and how often it won; it gives no CBR-specific benchmark. — https://www.percona.com/blog/percona-server-for-mongodb-8-3-technical-preview-is-now-available/ · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, explain plan, Cost-Based Ranker and Multi-Planning Changes (8.3 and 9.0)
- [fact] Merge location rules: if the pipeline starts with an exact $match on the shard key and has no $out or $lookup, the whole pipeline runs on the one matching shard (no split); otherwise results merge on mongos, except $out/$lookup cases and a randomly selected shard when a sort or group stage runs with allowDiskUse enabled. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v7.0/core/aggregation-pipeline-sharded-collections/ · keywords: explain plan, sharded explain, Sharded Explain and Split Pipelines (SHARD_MERGE and per-shard stats and merge shard selection)
- [passage] | Counter | Description | | --- | --- | | `collscan``clusteredCollscan` | Collection scans, counted separately based on whether the scan uses the [clustered index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#std-label-clustered-collections) | | `coveredIxscan` | Index scans that don't fetch documents. | | `ixscanFetch` | Index scans that fetch documents. | | `countScan` | Scans that count index keys without returning documents. | | `distinctScan``distinctScanFetch` | Scans that skip duplicate index keys, counted separately based on whether the scan fetches documents. | | `geoNear2d``geoNear2dSphere` | Geospatial proximity searches, counted separately based on whether the query uses a [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index) or [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index) index. | | `textMatch` | Text searches that use a [text index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#std-label-index-type-text) | | `otherAccessPath` | Winning plans that don't use a collection scan, an index scan, a count scan, a distinct scan, or a geospatial access path. A plan that only performs a text search increments both `textMatch` and `otherAccessPath`. | | `btreeIxscan``wildcardIxscan``sparseIxscan``uniqueIxscan``hashedIxscan``multikeyIxscan` | Index scans, counted separately by index property. A single index scan can increment multiple of these counters. | | `boundsFullScan``boundsPoint``boundsBoundedRange``boundsMinKeyToValue``boundsValueToMaxKey``boundsMixture` | Index scans, counted separately by the index bounds that the scan uses. MongoDB increments `boundsMixture` when the scan uses more than one type of bound. | | `boundsUnionedSmall``boundsUnionedLarge` | Index scans where a field has multiple bounds, counted separately by the number of bounds. `boundsUnionedSmall` counts fields with 2 to 50 bounds, and `boundsUnionedLarge` counts fields with 51 or more bounds. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md#access-path-counters · keywords: DISTINCT_SCAN, explain plan, collscan, clusteredCollscan, coveredIxscan, ixscanFetch
- [fact] Official $group docs advise: if a pipeline sorts and groups on the same field and $group uses only $first/$last, add an index on the grouped field matching the sort order. They also say $group of the form {_id:'$<field>'} can result in DISTINCT_SCAN, and to confirm via explain results. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md · keywords: DISTINCT_SCAN, explain plan, $group $first Loose Index Scan (DISTINCT_SCAN for sort-group-first)
- [passage] - Use an index to satisfy the sort so that MongoDB doesn't sort documents in memory. To learn more, see [Sort and Index Use.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#std-label-sort-index-use) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#per-operation-memory-limit · keywords: spill statistics
- [passage] - Filter documents with [`$match`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-match) as early as possible in the pipeline so that later stages process fewer documents. To learn more, see [Aggregation Pipeline Optimization.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#std-label-agg-pipeline-optimization) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#per-operation-memory-limit · keywords: spill statistics, $match
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.3, multi-planning with a cost-based ranker backup is the default plan selection mechanism for eligible queries. For a short trial period, the multi-planner attempts to find a plan capable of returning a result within the timeframe. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#query-plan-options · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker
- [passage] When explain is run in either executionStats or allPlansExecution verbosity mode, certain aggregation stages that may spill to disk have additional output. These stages include $sort, $group, $setWindowFields, $bucketAuto, $graphLookup, and $lookup (when using the slot-based execution engine). Starting in MongoDB 8.1, this also includes $text queries that use the TextOr execution stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: mongodb-advanced-explain-and-planner-changes
- [passage] The Explain Plan doesn't show aggregation pipeline stages such as [`$merge`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-merge) and [`$out`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/out.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-out) because Atlas ignores all out stages from the aggregation before running the explain plan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/query-plan.md#about-this-task · keywords: $merge, $out · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/query-plan.md
- [passage] Each field has the form `{ "value": <value>, "source": <string> }`. When you set a query knob with the [`setQuerySettings`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) command, MongoDB sets the `source` value to `"querySettings"`. When you set a query knob with [`setParameter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setparameter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setParameter), MongoDB sets the `source` value to `"setParameter"`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#query-knobs · keywords: cost-based ranker, { "value": <value>, "source": <string> }, setQuerySettings, source, "querySettings", setParameter
- [passage] The [`$search`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/aggregation-stages/search.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-search) aggregation stage is not restricted to 100 megabytes of RAM because it runs in a separate process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#memory-restrictions · keywords: spill statistics, $search · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
- [passage] - Using `{ allowDiskUse: true }` to allow writing temporary files out to disk when `allowDiskUseByDefault` is set to `false` — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: spill statistics, { allowDiskUse: true }, allowDiskUseByDefault, false · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sortByCount.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.aggregate.md
- [passage] - Using `{ allowDiskUse: false }` to prohibit writing temporary files out to disk when `allowDiskUseByDefault` is set to `true` — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: spill statistics, { allowDiskUse: false }, allowDiskUseByDefault, true · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sortByCount.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.aggregate.md
- [passage] When [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) generates index keys on a field that holds an array, [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) generates an index key for each array element. For compound indexes, [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) calculates the [cartesian product](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-cartesian-product) of the sets of keys that are generated for each field. If both sets are large, then calculating the cartesian product could cause the operation to exceed memory limits. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md#indexes · keywords: spill statistics, mongod
- [passage] In some instances, such as when running in a container that is configured to use less RAM than the amount of memory provisioned for the host, you must account for the limits. You may need to configure the WiredTiger cache to an appropriate value, as WiredTiger may not account for the memory limits of the specific container in certain cases. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#wiredtiger-options · keywords: spill statistics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/production-notes.md
- [passage] usedDisk is true when the query writes data to temporary files due to memory restrictions. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: spill statistics
- [passage] A query that exceeds either 100 megabytes or the available memory spills to disk. It writes intermediate data to storage to save memory, which can cause lowered performance. Use the [`allowDiskUseByDefault`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) parameter or [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) method to configure this behavior. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents.md#query-spill · keywords: spill statistics, allowDiskUseByDefault, cursor.allowDiskUse()
- [passage] - If the deployment is a sharded cluster, a shard removal may cause an open change stream cursor to close. The closed change stream cursor may not be fully resumable. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.watch.md#behavior · keywords: mongodb-advanced-explain-and-planner-changes
- [passage] For example, `$group` operations of the following form can result in a `DISTINCT_SCAN`: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md#retrieve-distinct-values · keywords: DISTINCT_SCAN, $group
- [passage] When run without [localOps:true](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#std-label-currentOp-stage-localOps) on the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos), the transaction information is per shard. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentOp.md#mongos-composite-view-output · keywords: sharded explain, mongos
- [passage] When run on a [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) without [localOps:true](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#std-label-currentOp-stage-localOps), the transaction information is per shard. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentOp.md#mongos-per-shard-output · keywords: sharded explain, mongos
- [passage] When run on a [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos), [`$currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-currentOp) returns the opids in the format of `"<shardName>:<opid on that shard>"`; e.g. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.killOp.md#kill-write-operations · keywords: sharded explain, mongos, $currentOp, "<shardName>:<opid on that shard>"
- [passage] After the mongos receives responses from all shards, it merges the data and returns the result document. The performance of a broadcast operation depends on the overall load of the cluster, as well as variables like network latency, individual shard load, and number of documents returned per shard. Whenever possible, favor operations that result in targeted operation over those that result in a broadcast operation. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: sharded explain · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] To see whether your operation results in a `DISTINCT_SCAN`, check your operation's [explain results.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-results) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md#retrieve-distinct-values · keywords: DISTINCT_SCAN, explain plan
- [passage] To determine whether a pipeline uses indexes, review the query plan and look for `IXSCAN` or `DISTINCT_SCAN` plans. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#indexes · keywords: DISTINCT_SCAN, explain plan, IXSCAN
- [passage] To check per-operation memory usage, use these [`serverStatus`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverstatus.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.serverStatus) metrics: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md#operations · keywords: spill statistics, serverStatus
- [passage] To learn more about memory limits, see [Memory Use.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger.md#std-label-wiredtiger-RAM) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#wiredtiger-options · keywords: spill statistics
- [passage] To analyze query performance, see Interpret Explain Plan Results. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: mongodb-advanced-explain-and-planner-changes
- [passage] To help you better understand the performance of your pipeline, you can view your pipeline's explain plan. You can view the explain plan at any point while creating or editing your pipeline. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/agg-pipeline-builder/view-pipeline-explain-plan.md · keywords: mongodb-advanced-explain-and-planner-changes
- [passage] To learn more, see Query Knobs. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: cost-based ranker

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Starting in MongoDB 9.0 a per-operation memory limit (internalQueryMaxMemoryUsageBytesPerOperation, default max of 1 GB or 20% of server memory) covers combined tracked memory of blocking stages and expressions. It does not change per-stage spilling. Overruns return QueryExceededMemoryLimitNoDiskUseAllowed (292, when allowDiskUse is false) or ExceededMemoryLimit (146). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, aggregation explain, explain plan, spill statistics, Aggregation Explain and Spill Statistics ($lookup and $group and memory limits)
- [passage] | **MongoDB Version** | **Changes** | | --- | --- | | 6.1 | Slow operation log messages include [cache refresh time fields.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-cache-refresh-times) | | 6.2 | Slow operation log messages include a `queryFramework` field that indicates which query engine executed the query: `queryFramework: "classic"` indicates that the classic engine executed the query.; `queryFramework: "sbe"` indicates that the slot-based query execution engine executed the query. | | 6.3 | Slow operation log messages and [database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) entries include a `cpuNanos` field that specifies the total CPU time spent by a query operation in nanoseconds. The `cpuNanos` field is only available on Linux systems. | | 7.0 (and 6.0.13, 5.0.24) | The `totalOplogSlotDurationMicros` in the slow query log message shows the time between a write operation getting a commit timestamp to commit the storage engine writes and actually committing. `mongod` supports parallel writes. However, it commits write operations with commit timestamps in any order. For example, consider the following writes with commit timestamps: writeA with Timestamp1; writeB with Timestamp2; writeC with Timestamp3 Suppose writeB commits first at Timestamp2. Replication is paused until writeA commits because writeA's oplog entry with Timestamp1 is required for replication to copy the oplog to secondary replica set members. | | 8.0 | The slow query output includes a `queues` document that contains information about the operation's [queues](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverstatus.md#std-label-server-status-queues). Each queue in the `queues` field contains a `totalTimeQueuedMicros` field that contains the total cumulative time in microseconds that the operation spent in the corresponding queue. The `queryShapeHash` field for a [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes) is also included in the slow query log when available. If a command with a specific query shape is [rejected](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/operation-rejection-filters.md#std-label-operation-rejection-filters), MongoDB logs a message that states the query command was rejected. The message contains the query namespace, `queryShapeHash`, and the command with the rejected query. MongoDB only logs the message if the log verbosity level is set to at least `2`. | | 8.1 | Slow query log messages contain new metrics if the query execution writes temporary files to disk. These metrics are prefixed by the query execution stage that caused the query to exceed the memory limit. For example, `sortSpills` indicates the number of times that the sort stage of query execution wrote temporary files to disk. `<executionPart>Spills` indicates the number of times the corresponding query execution stage wrote temporary files to disk.; `<executionPart>SpilledBytes` indicates the size, in bytes, of the memory released by writing temporary files to disk.; `<executionPart>SpilledDataStorageSize` indicates the size, in bytes, of disk space used for temporary files.; `<executionPart>SpilledRecords` indicates the number of records written to temporary files on disk. For more information on writing temporary files to disk, see [`allowDiskUse()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) | | 8.3 | Slow query log entries have an optional `originalQueryShapeHash` field that contains that query shape of the following operations that originate on the [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#std-program-mongos) : [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find); [`aggregate`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.aggregate); [`count`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/count.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.count); [`distinct`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.distinct) The original query shape of the `mongos` operation may differ after the `mongos` sends the operation to the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#std-program-mongod) . MongoDB 8.3 also introduces slow in-progress query log entries. Queries trigger a slow-in progress log during execution. These logs contain less information than standard slow query logs. MongoDB logs queries at most once if the query's duration surpasses the [`operationProfiling.slowOpInProgressThresholdMs`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpInProgressThresholdMs) When an operation specifies a [time limit for a query](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents/specify-query-timeout.md#std-label-manual-query-timeout), slow query logs contain a `deadline` field. `deadline` indicates the time the operation must complete by, which is equal to the time at the start of the operation plus the value of the query timeout. | | 9.0 | When a query shape has query knobs set through [`setQuerySettings`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) or [`setParameter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setparameter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setParameter), slow query log entries include a `queryKnobs` document. The document shows the effective value of each knob and where the value comes from, with the same shape as the [explain output](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-output-query-knobs). For details, see [Query Knobs.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#std-label-setQuerySettings-query-knobs) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#version-specific-changes · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, explain plan, spill statistics, queryFramework, queryFramework: "classic"
- [fact] Since MongoDB 6.0 the allowDiskUseByDefault parameter decides whether stages needing more than 100 MB of memory write temporary files (true) or raise an error (false). Per-command {allowDiskUse: true|false} overrides it. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md · keywords: aggregation explain, explain plan, spill statistics, Aggregation Explain and Spill Statistics ($lookup and $group and memory limits)
- [fact] $push and $addToSet inside $group cannot spill: each hits a separate 100 MB cap and fails with 'used too much memory and cannot spill to disk. Memory limit: 104857600 bytes' even with allowDiskUse: true. Fix by restructuring (filter or limit first, two-step group, $topN), not by flag. — https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-exceeded-memory-limit-group-sort/ · keywords: aggregation explain, explain plan, spill statistics, Aggregation Explain and Spill Statistics ($lookup and $group and memory limits)
- [fact] Profiler and diagnostic log lines carry a usedDisk indicator when any stage wrote temporary files, so spills show up in slow-query logs without re-running explain. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md · keywords: aggregation explain, explain plan, spill statistics, Aggregation Explain and Spill Statistics ($lookup and $group and memory limits)
- [fact] Mitigations for memory pressure: use an index-backed sort, put $limit after $sort, and filter with $match early. On sharded clusters, allowDiskUse on a sorting or grouping stage may move the merge to a randomly selected shard. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md · keywords: aggregation explain, explain plan, spill statistics, Aggregation Explain and Spill Statistics ($lookup and $group and memory limits)

Batch size specifies the maximum number of documents that can be returned in each batch of a query result. By default, the initial batch size is the lesser of `101` documents or 16 mebibytes (MiB) worth of documents. Subsequent batches have a maximum size of 16 MiB. `batchSize` can enforce a smaller limit than 16 MiB, but not a larger one. This field is only available on Linux systems. **New in version 8.2** | | `metrics``.cpuNanos``.max` | NumberLong | Literal | Maximum CPU time spent on a query operation in nanoseconds. This field is only available on Linux systems. **New in version 8.2** | | `metrics``.cpuNanos``.min` | NumberLong | Literal | Minimum CPU time spent on a query operation in nanoseconds. This field is only available on Linux systems. **New in version 8.2** | | `metrics``.cpuNanos``.sumOfSquares` | NumberDecimal | Literal | Sum of squares of CPU time spent on query operations. This field is only available on Linux systems. A high `sumOfSquares` value indicates high variance in the CPU time for individual queries. **New in version 8.2** | | `metrics``.clusterPeakTrackedMemBytes` | NumberLong | Literal | Sum of local peak tracked memory and sum of peak tracked memory from all remote shards contacted during query execution. **New in version 9.0** | | `metrics``.peakTrackedMemBytes` | NumberLong | Literal | Peak local tracked memory usage. **New in version 9.0** | | `metrics``.planningTimeMicros` | Document | Literal | Contains metrics related to the time spent during query planning for queries with the given key. All `planningTimeMicros` subfields are reported in microseconds. **New in version 8.3** | | `metrics``.planningTimeMicros``.sum` | NumberLong | Literal | Total query planning time. **New in version 8.3** | | `metrics``.planningTimeMicros``.max` | NumberLong | Literal | Maximum query planning time. **New in version 8.3** | | `metrics``.planningTimeMicros``.min` | NumberLong | Literal | Minimum query planning time. **New in version 8.3** | | `metrics``.planningTimeMicros``.sumOfSquares` | NumberDecimal | Literal | Sum of squares of query planning times. - [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `distinct` | string | The name of the collection to query for distinct values. | | `key` | string | The field for which to return distinct values. | | `query` | document | Optional. A query that specifies the documents from which to retrieve the distinct values. | | `readConcern` | document | Optional. Specifies the [read concern.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-read-concern) The `readConcern` option has the following syntax: `readConcern: { level: <value> }` Possible read concern levels are: [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-). This is the default read concern level for read operations against the primary and secondaries.; [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-). Available for read operations against the primary and secondaries. [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-) behaves the same as [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-) against the primary and non-sharded secondaries. The query returns the instance's most recent data.; [`"majority"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-majority.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-majority-). Available for replica sets that use [WiredTiger storage engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger.md#std-label-storage-wiredtiger); [`"linearizable"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-linearizable.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-linearizable-). Available for read operations on the [`primary`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-states.md#mongodb-replstate-replstate.PRIMARY) only.; [`"snapshot"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-snapshot-). Available for [multi-document transactions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md#std-label-transactions) and certain read operations outside of multi-document transactions. For more formation on the read concern levels, see [Read Concern Levels.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern.md#std-label-read-concern-levels) | | `collation` | document | Optional. Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) If the collation is unspecified but the collection has a default collation (see [`db.createCollection()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#mongodb-method-db.createCollection)), the operation uses the collation specified for the collection. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. Once set, this comment appears alongside records of this command in the following locations: [mongod log messages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-ref), in the `attr.command.cursor.comment` field.; [Database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.command) field.; [`currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.currentOp) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-data-currentOp.command) field. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). | | `hint` | string or document | Optional. Specify the index name, either as a string or a document. If specified, the query planner only considers plans using the hinted index. For more details, see [Specify an Index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct.md#std-label-index-example) **New in version 7.1** | | `querySettings` | document | Optional. Query settings that apply only to this execution of the command. The `querySettings` document accepts the following fields: `indexHints`; `queryFramework`; `reject`; `comment`; `queryKnobs`; `maxTimeMS` For descriptions of these fields, see [Command Fields.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#std-label-setQuerySettings-fields) MongoDB doesn't store these settings on the cluster, and they don't apply to other queries with the same [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes). To set query settings that persist for a query shape, use [`setQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) MongoDB combines the settings that you pass in the command with any query settings stored on the cluster for the same query shape. If both settings specify the same field, the stored cluster setting takes precedence. **New in version 9.0** | | `maxTimeMS` | non-negative integer | Optional. Specifies a time limit in milliseconds. MongoDB terminates operations that exceed their allotted time limit using the same mechanism as [`db.killOp()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.killop.md#mongodb-method-db.killOp). MongoDB only terminates an operation at one of its designated [interrupt points.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-interrupt-point) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct.md#command-fields · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, distinct, key, query, readConcern

- [passage] If MongoDB cannot obtain the sort order with an index scan, then MongoDB uses a top-k sort algorithm. This algorithm buffers the first `k` results (or last, depending on the sort order) seen so far by the underlying index or collection access. If the memory footprint of these `k` results exceeds 100 megabytes, MongoDB automatically writes temporary files to disk unless the query specifies [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) with a value of `false` (in which case, the query fails). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#limit-results · keywords: spill statistics, cursor.allowDiskUse(), false
- [passage] createIndexes supports building one or more indexes on a collection. createIndexes uses a combination of memory and temporary files on disk to build indexes. In self-hosted MongoDB deployments, the default value of the maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes parameter is 200 megabytes per createIndexes command. createIndexes shares the memory limit equally among all the indexes it builds. For example, if you build 10 indexes with one createIndexes command, MongoDB allocates each index 20 megabytes for the index build process. When you reach the memory limit, MongoDB creates temporary files in the _tmp subdirectory within --dbpath to complete the build. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: spill statistics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] In self-hosted MongoDB deployments, you can change the memory limit for index builds by setting the maxIndexBuildMemoryUsageMegabytes parameter. Increasing this parameter is only necessary in rare cases. Such cases include running many simultaneous index builds with a single createIndexes command or indexing a data set larger than 500GB. You can also set maxNumActiveUserIndexBuilds to adjust how many index builds can run concurrently. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: spill statistics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md

Use this metric to determine whether the memory limit is too low for your workload. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#metrics · keywords: spill statistics
- [passage] Largest amount of memory in bytes tracked for a single operation since startup. Use this metric to determine an appropriate per-operation memory limit for your workload. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#metrics · keywords: spill statistics
- [passage] An [initial sync](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md#std-label-replica-set-sync) populates only one collection at a time and has no risk of exceeding the memory limit. However, it is possible for a user to start index builds on multiple collections in multiple databases simultaneously. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md#indexes · keywords: spill statistics
- [passage] To view the [`memory limit`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/hostinfo.md#mongodb-data-hostInfo.system.memLimitMB), the value that WiredTiger utilizes as the maximum amount of RAM available use the [`hostInfo`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/hostinfo.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.hostInfo) command. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#wiredtiger-options · keywords: spill statistics, memory limit, hostInfo · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/production-notes.md
- [passage] The [`$bucket`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bucket.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-bucket) stage has a limit of 100 megabytes of RAM. By default, if the stage exceeds this limit, [`$bucket`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bucket.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-bucket) returns an error. To allow more space for stage processing, use the [allowDiskUse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md#std-label-aggregate-cmd-allowDiskUse) option to enable aggregation pipeline stages to write data to temporary files. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bucket.md#bucket-and-memory-restrictions · keywords: spill statistics, $bucket
- [passage] When a [`$sort`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-sort) precedes a [`$limit`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/limit.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-limit) and there are no intervening stages that modify the number of documents, the optimizer can coalesce the [`$limit`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/limit.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-limit) into the [`$sort`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-sort). This allows the [`$sort`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-sort) operation to only maintain the top `n` results as it progresses, where `n` is the specified limit, and ensures that MongoDB only needs to store `n` items in memory. This optimization still applies when `allowDiskUse` is `true` and the `n` items exceed the [aggregation memory limit.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#std-label-agg-memory-restrictions) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#sort-and-limit-memory-optimization · keywords: spill statistics, $sort, $limit,  results as it progresses, where ,  items in memory. This optimization still applies when ,  is  · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/limit.md
- [passage] The [`$bucketAuto`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bucketauto.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-bucketAuto) stage has a limit of 100 megabytes of RAM. By default, if the stage exceeds this limit, MongoDB automatically writes temporary files to disk. For details, see [`allowDiskUseByDefault`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/bucketAuto.md#bucketauto-and-memory-restrictions · keywords: spill statistics, $bucketAuto, allowDiskUseByDefault
- [passage] - A single [`$accumulator`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md#mongodb-group-grp.-accumulator) operation exceeds its specified memory limit. If you specify the [`allowDiskUse`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.aggregate.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.aggregate) option, the operator stores the in-progress operation on disk and finishes the operation in memory. Once the operation finishes, the results from disk and memory are merged together using the [merge](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md#std-label-accumulator-merge) function. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/accumulator.md#merge-two-states-with-merge · keywords: spill statistics, $accumulator, allowDiskUse
- [passage] Slow query log messages contain new metrics if the query execution writes temporary files to disk. These metrics are prefixed by the query execution stage that caused the query to exceed the memory limit. For example, sortSpills indicates the number of times that the sort stage of query execution wrote temporary files to disk. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: spill statistics
- [passage] "msg": "Query exceeded the memory limit", — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: spill statistics
- [passage] "error": "expression evaluation needs too much memory. Needs: 1140850688 bytes. Local memory limit: 1073741824 bytes. Global memory used: 1140850688 bytes. Global memory limit: 1073741824 bytes." — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: spill statistics
- [passage] The error attribute is a string that contains the details of the memory overage. The details include the operation that exceeded the limit, the amount of memory in use, and the applicable memory limit. MongoDB also returns this string to the client in the ExceededMemoryLimit error. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: spill statistics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md
- [passage] MongoDB writes this log message only when an operation exceeds the per-operation memory limit and cannot spill to disk. If a stage that can spill to disk exceeds the limit and allowDiskUse is false, MongoDB ends the operation with the QueryExceededMemoryLimitNoDiskUseAllowed error and does not write this log message. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: spill statistics · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md
- [passage] To learn how MongoDB limits memory usage during aggregation, see [Per-Operation Memory Limit.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#std-label-operation-memory-limit) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#aggregation-stages-with-expression-memory-tracking · keywords: spill statistics
- [passage] To learn how MongoDB limits memory usage during aggregation, see Per-Operation Memory Limit. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: spill statistics
- [fact] Index key order must fit the group key: the index {user:1,timestamp:-1,request:1} did not give DISTINCT_SCAN for $group by request after $sort by timestamp. Reindexing to {user:1,request:1,timestamp:-1} with $sort {request:1,timestamp:-1} did, but the output came back ordered by request. A MongoDB engineer's fix was a second $sort by timestamp after $group, followed by $limit, which the optimizer coalesces into a top-k. — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/poor-performance-of-getting-most-recent-distinct-values-full-index-scan/208264 · keywords: DISTINCT_SCAN, $group $first Loose Index Scan (DISTINCT_SCAN for sort-group-first)

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `find` | string | The name of the collection or [view](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views.md#std-label-views-landing-page) to query. | | `filter` | document | Optional. The query predicate. If unspecified, all documents in the collection match the predicate. | | [sort](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-cmd-sort) | document | Optional. The sort specification for the ordering of the results. | | `projection` | document | Optional. The [projection specification](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/project-fields-from-query-results.md#std-label-projections) to determine which fields to include in the returned documents. [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) operations on views do not support the following [find command projection operators:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/projection.md#std-label-projection-operators-ref) [`$`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/positional.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-); [`$elemMatch`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/elemmatch.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-elemMatch); [`$slice`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/projection/slice.md#mongodb-projection-proj.-slice); [`$meta`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/meta.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-meta) | | `hint` | string or document | Optional. Index specification. Specify either the index name as a string or the index key pattern. If specified, the query system only considers plans using the hinted index. With the following exception, `hint` is required if the command includes the `min` or `max` fields. `hint` is not required with `min` or `max` if the `filter` is an equality condition on the `_id` field `{ _id: <value> }`. | | `skip` | positive integer | Optional. Number of documents to skip. Defaults to 0. | | `limit` | non-negative integer | Optional. The maximum number of documents to return. If unspecified, then defaults to no limit. A limit of 0 is equivalent to setting no limit. | | `batchSize` | non-negative integer | Optional. The maximum number of documents that can be returned in each batch of a query result. By default, the `find` command has an initial `batchSize` of the lesser of `101` documents or 16 mebibytes (MiB) worth of documents. Subsequent batches have a maximum size of 16 MiB. This option can enforce a smaller limit than 16 MiB, but not a larger one. When set, the `batchSize` is the lesser of `batchSize` documents or 16 MiB worth of documents. A `batchSize` of `0` means that the cursor is established, but no documents are returned in the first batch. Unlike the previous wire protocol version, a batchSize of 1 for the [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) command does not close the cursor. To specify batch size for subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) operations, use [`batchSize()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.batchsize.md#mongodb-method-cursor.batchSize) in mongosh. | | `singleBatch` | boolean | Optional. Determines whether to close the cursor after the first batch. Defaults to false. | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. Once set, this comment appears alongside records of this command in the following locations: [mongod log messages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-ref), in the `attr.command.cursor.comment` field.; [Database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.command) field.; [`currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.currentOp) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-data-currentOp.command) field. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). Any comment set on a `find` command is inherited by any subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) commands run on the `find` cursor. | | `maxTimeMS` | non-negative integer | Optional. Specifies a time limit in milliseconds. If you do not specify a value for `maxTimeMS`, operations will not time out. A value of `0` explicitly specifies the default unbounded behavior. MongoDB terminates operations that exceed their allotted time limit using the same mechanism as [`db.killOp()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.killop.md#mongodb-method-db.killOp). MongoDB only terminates an operation at one of its designated [interrupt points.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-interrupt-point) When specifying [`linearizable read concern`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-linearizable.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-linearizable-), always use `maxTimeMS` in case a majority of data bearing members are unavailable. `maxTimeMS` ensures that the operation does not block indefinitely and instead returns an error if the read concern cannot be fulfilled. [`maxTimeMS()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxtimems.md#mongodb-method-cursor.maxTimeMS) is unrelated to [`noCursorTimeout()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.nocursortimeout.md#mongodb-method-cursor.noCursorTimeout). [`maxTimeMS()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxtimems.md#mongodb-method-cursor.maxTimeMS) limits processing time, while [`noCursorTimeout()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.nocursortimeout.md#mongodb-method-cursor.noCursorTimeout) prevents idle-time expiration. A cursor's idle time does not contribute to its processing time. | | `readConcern` | document | Optional. Specifies the [read concern.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-read-concern) The `readConcern` option has the following syntax: `readConcern: { level: <value> }` Possible read concern levels are: [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-). This is the default read concern level for read operations against the primary and secondaries.; [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-). Available for read operations against the primary and secondaries. [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-) behaves the same as [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-) against the primary and non-sharded secondaries. The query returns the instance's most recent data.; [`"majority"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-majority.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-majority-). Available for replica sets that use [WiredTiger storage engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger.md#std-label-storage-wiredtiger); [`"linearizable"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-linearizable.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-linearizable-). Available for read operations on the [`primary`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-states.md#mongodb-replstate-replstate.PRIMARY) only.; [`"snapshot"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-snapshot-). Available for [multi-document transactions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md#std-label-transactions) and certain read operations outside of multi-document transactions. For more formation on the read concern levels, see [Read Concern Levels.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern.md#std-label-read-concern-levels) The [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) command uses the `readConcern` level specified in the originating `find` command. | | `max` | document | Optional. The *exclusive* upper bound for a specific index. See [`cursor.max()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md#mongodb-method-cursor.max) for details. To use the `max` field, the command must also use `hint` unless the specified `filter` is an equality condition on the `_id` field `{ _id: <value> }`. | | `min` | document | Optional. The *inclusive* lower bound for a specific index. See [`cursor.min()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#mongodb-method-cursor.min) for details. To use the `min` field, the command must also use `hint` unless the specified `filter` is an equality condition on the `_id` field `{ _id: <value> }`. | | `returnKey` | boolean | Optional. If true, returns only the index keys in the resulting documents. Defaults to false. If returnKey is true and the [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) command does not use an index, the returned documents are empty. | | `showRecordId` | boolean | Optional. Determines whether to return the record identifier for each document. If true, adds a field $recordId to the returned documents. | | `tailable` | boolean | Optional. Returns a [tailable cursor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-tailable-cursor) for a capped collections. | | `awaitData` | boolean | Optional. Use with the tailable option to block a [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) command on the cursor temporarily at the end of data rather than returning no data. After a timeout period, [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) returns as normal. | | `noCursorTimeout` | boolean | Optional. Prevents the server from timing out non-session idle cursors after an inactivity period of 30 minutes. Ignored for cursors that are part of a session. For more information, see [Session Idle Timeout.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-session-idle-timeout) | | [allowPartialResults](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-cmd-find-allowPartialResults) | boolean | Optional. For queries against a sharded collection, allows the command (or subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) commands) to return partial results instead of an error if one or more queried shards are unavailable. If [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) (or subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) commands) returns partial results because the queried shard(s) aren't available, the [find output](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-cmd-find-output) includes a `partialResultsReturned` indicator field. If the queried shards are available for the initial `find` command, but one or more shards become unavailable for subsequent `getMore` commands, only the `getMore` commands that run while the shards aren't available include `partialResultsReturned` in their output. | | `collation` | document | Optional. Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) If the collation is unspecified but the collection has a default collation (see [`db.createCollection()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#mongodb-method-db.createCollection)), the operation uses the collation specified for the collection. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. | | [allowDiskUse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-cmd-allowDiskUse) | boolean | Optional. Use this option to override [`allowDiskUseByDefault`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) for a specific query. You can use this option to either: Prohibit disk use on a system where disk use is allowed by default.; Allow disk use on a system where disk use is prohibited by default. Starting in MongoDB 6.0, if [`allowDiskUseByDefault`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) is set to `true` and the server requires more than 100 megabytes of memory for a pipeline execution stage, MongoDB automatically writes temporary files to disk unless the query specifies `{ allowDiskUse: false }`. For details, see [`allowDiskUseByDefault`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) `allowDiskUse` has no effect if MongoDB can satisfy the specified [sort](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-cmd-sort) using an index, *or* if the in-memory sort requires less than 100 megabytes of memory. For more complete documentation on `allowDiskUse`, see [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) For more information on memory restrictions for large in-memory sorts, see [Sort and Index Use.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#std-label-sort-index-use) | | [let](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-let-syntax) | document | Optional. Specifies a document with a list of variables. This allows you to improve command readability by separating the variables from the query text. The document syntax is: `{ <variable_name_1>: <expression_1>, ..., <variable_name_n>: <expression_n> }` The variable is set to the value returned by the expression, and cannot be changed afterwards. To access the value of a variable in the command, use the double dollar sign prefix (`$$`) together with your variable name in the form `$$<variable_name>`. For example: `$$targetTotal`. To use a variable to filter results, you must access the variable within the [`$expr`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#mongodb-query-op.-expr) operator. For a complete example using `let` and variables, see [Use Variables in `let`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-let-example) **New in version 5.0** | | `querySettings` | document | Optional. Query settings that apply only to this execution of the command. The `querySettings` document accepts the following fields: `indexHints`; `queryFramework`; `reject`; `comment`; `queryKnobs`; `maxTimeMS` For descriptions of these fields, see [Command Fields.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#std-label-setQuerySettings-fields) MongoDB doesn't store these settings on the cluster, and they don't apply to other queries with the same [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes). To set query settings that persist for a query shape, use [`setQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) MongoDB combines the settings that you pass in the command with any query settings stored on the cluster for the same query shape. If both settings specify the same field, the stored cluster setting takes precedence. **New in version 9.0** | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#command-fields · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, spill statistics, find, filter, projection
- [passage] | Field | Field Type | Necessity | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `setQuerySettings` | document or string | Required | You can provide either: The same fields as those in a [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find), [`distinct`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.distinct), or [`aggregate`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.aggregate) command, and a `$db` field with the database associated with the original command.; An existing query shape hash string that uniquely identifies the query shape. An example query shape hash is `"F42757F1AEB68B4C5A6DE6182B29B01947C829C926BCC01226BDA4DDE799766C"``. | | `indexHints.ns` | document | Optional | Namespace for index hints. Only required when optional index hints are specified. | | `indexHints.ns.db` | string | Conditional | Name of the database for the index hints. Required when you specify `indexHints.ns`. | | `indexHints.ns.coll` | string | Conditional | Name of the collection for the index hints. Required when you specify `indexHints.ns`. | | `indexHints.allowedIndexes` | array | Optional | Array of indexes for index hints. An index hint can be one of these: Index name; index key pattern; [`$natural`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-operator-metaOp.-natural) hint For more details, see [Indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/indexes.md#std-label-indexes) and [`hint()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) | | `queryFramework` | string | Optional | [Query framework](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-framework) string can be set to: `classic` to use the classic engine.; `sbe` to use slot-based query execution engine. For details, see [Slot-Based Query Execution Engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/sbe.md#std-label-sbe-landing) | | `reject` | boolean | Optional | If `true`: New queries with the matching query shape are rejected and the query response states the query is rejected.; Any queries currently in progress aren't rejected. Default is `false`. To enable a query shape, run `setQuerySettings` again for the query shape and set `reject` to `false`. If you set `reject` to `true` and then back to `false` using `setQuerySettings` then: If your `settings` document isn't empty, then `setQuerySettings` enables the query shape.; If your `settings` document only contains `reject: false`, then `setQuerySettings` returns an error. Instead, use the `removeQuerySettings` command to remove the settings and then use `setQuerySettings` to add query settings. | | `comment` | BSON type | Optional | A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types). For example: string, object, and so on. You can use a comment to provide additional information about the query settings. For example, to add a string that indicates why you added the query settings, use `comment: "Index hint for orderDate_1 index to improve query performance"`. To update a comment, run `setQuerySettings` again and use `comment: { body: { msg: "Updated comment" } }`. You cannot remove a comment, but you can set it to a string with a space character. You can remove the query settings using [`removeQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/removequerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.removeQuerySettings) Comments appear in the [`$querySettings`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/querysettings.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-querySettings) aggregation pipeline stage output, the [explain() command output](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-results), and the [slow query logs.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-message-slow-ops) **New in version 8.1** (and 8.0.4). | | `queryKnobs` | document | Optional | A document of `{ <knobName>: <value> }` pairs that override internal server parameters for this query shape only, instead of instance-wide with [`setParameter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setparameter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setParameter). Each knob keeps the type, bounds, and default of its underlying server parameter. Unlike the other `setQuerySettings` fields, which replace the entire value when set, `queryKnobs` merges with existing knob values. `setQuerySettings` changes the knobs you include in the `queryKnobs` document, and leaves all other knobs unchanged. `queryKnobs: {}` results in a no-op. To remove a single knob without affecting the others, set that knob's value to `null`. **New in version 9.0** | | `maxTimeMS` | non-negative integer | Optional | Sets a time limit in milliseconds for executions of the [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes). Use this setting to cap a single regressed shape or lift an over-tight client timeout without changing application code. If you omit `maxTimeMS` from query settings, the operation's timeout follows the command-level `maxTimeMS` option and the [`defaultMaxTimeMS`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/cluster-parameters/defaultmaxtimems.md#mongodb-parameter-param.defaultMaxTimeMS) cluster parameter. Setting `maxTimeMS` to `0` clears the `maxTimeMS` query setting, and the operation falls back to the command-level and cluster default values. A `maxTimeMS` value set with `setQuerySettings` takes precedence over a `maxTimeMS` value supplied in the command. **New in version 9.0** | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#command-fields · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, explain plan, setQuerySettings, find, distinct

For details, see [`cursor.allowDiskUse()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.allowdiskuse.md#mongodb-method-cursor.allowDiskUse) | | allowPartialResults | For queries against a sharded collection, allows the command (or subsequent getMore commands) to return partial results, rather than an error, if one or more queried shards are unavailable. | | awaitData | If the cursor is a a tailable-await cursor. Requires `tailable` to be `true`. | | collation | Collation settings for update operation. | | comment | Adds a `$comment` to the query that shows in the [profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) logs. | | explain | Adds explain output based on the verbosity mode provided. | | hint | Forces the query optimizer to use specific indexes in the query. | | limit | Sets a limit of documents returned in the result set. | | max | The exclusive upper bound for a specific index. | | maxAwaitTimeMS | The maximum amount of time for the server to wait on new documents to satisfy a tailable cursor query.
