To use `options.projection`, set the `projection` parameter to `null` or `undefined`. | | readConcern | Specifies the read concern level for the query. | | readPreference | Specifies the read preference level for the query. | | returnKey | Whether only the index keys are returned for a query. | | showRecordId | If the `$recordId` field is added to the returned documents. - [passage] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, you can use the `queryKnobs` setting to override internal server parameters for a single [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes) instead of the whole instance. Set the `queryKnobs` field for targeted queries to mitigate the impact of one regressed shape without changing behavior for other workloads on the same deployment. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, queryKnobs
- [fact] CBR scores each plan node with a cost function and cardinality estimates and picks the plan with the lowest top-level costEstimate. The docs state MongoDB currently invokes CBR for only a small number of queries; eligibility rules and the continue-vs-CBR fallback rules are not published in the query-plans page. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/core/query-plans/ · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, Cost-Based Ranker and Multi-Planning Changes (8.3 and 9.0)

- [passage] For example, you can override the [`notablescan`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.notablescan) server parameter for a single query shape instead of the whole instance by setting `queryKnobs` to `{ noTableScan: true }`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: cost-based ranker, notablescan, queryKnobs, { noTableScan: true }
- [passage] Unlike [`setParameter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setparameter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setParameter), which applies per process and can differ between nodes, MongoDB applies the same `queryKnobs` values across the whole cluster for the matching query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: cost-based ranker, setParameter, queryKnobs
- [fact] Correctness bug SERVER-97238: with data {mk:[1,2,3], notMk:4}, index {notMk:1, mk:1}, and $group _id:$notMk acc:{$first:'$mk'}, a distinct scan returned acc:1 instead of [1,2,3]. The planner only checked for multikey fields before the distinct key, not the projected field. Affected 4.2 through 8.0; fixed in 8.1.0-rc0 (resolved 2025-02-08). On older servers, a $first over an array field covered by a multikey index entry is a result-correctness risk. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-97238 · keywords: DISTINCT_SCAN, $group $first Loose Index Scan (DISTINCT_SCAN for sort-group-first)
- [passage] - [`QueryExceededMemoryLimitNoDiskUseAllowed`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/error-codes.md#mongodb-error-292) when a stage that can spill to disk exceeds the limit and `allowDiskUse` is `false`. Run the operation with `{ allowDiskUse: true }` so that the stage spills to disk instead of failing. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-limits.md#per-operation-memory-limit · keywords: spill statistics, QueryExceededMemoryLimitNoDiskUseAllowed, allowDiskUse, false, { allowDiskUse: true } · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/limits.md
- [passage] Query knobs are part of the hashed query settings, so they are also part of the [plan cache key](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-plan-cache-key). If you change a knob value, MongoDB produces a new plan cache key, so the planner creates a fresh plan instead of reusing a stale cached plan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: cost-based ranker
- [passage] - On a sharded cluster if `$currentOp` is run with [localOps:true](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentop.md#std-label-currentOp-stage-localOps). The transaction information is a composite view rather than per shard. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentOp.md#output-fields · keywords: sharded explain, $currentOp
- [passage] For a collection in a replica set or a [non-sharded collection](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding.md#std-label-sharded-vs-non-sharded-collections) in a cluster, `$collStats` outputs a single document. For a [sharded collection](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding.md#std-label-sharded-vs-non-sharded-collections), `$collStats` outputs one document per shard. The output document includes the following fields: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/collStats.md#definition · keywords: sharded explain, $collStats
- [passage] `$collStats` outputs one document per shard when run on [sharded collections](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding.md#std-label-sharded-vs-non-sharded-collections). Each output document contains a `shard` field with the name of the shard the document corresponds to. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/collStats.md#collstats-on-sharded-collections · keywords: sharded explain, $collStats, shard
- [fact] A pipeline starting with $sort and then $group using only $first (or only $last) can be planned as a DISTINCT_SCAN over a matching index. It reads about one index entry per group instead of the whole index. The original ticket's example: index {x:1,y:1}, $sort {x:1,y:1}, $group by x with $first y, which previously did a full index scan. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-9507 · keywords: DISTINCT_SCAN, $group $first Loose Index Scan (DISTINCT_SCAN for sort-group-first)

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The explain results page also documents peakTrackedMemBytes (8.1 table) and, from MongoDB 9.0, expressionEvaluationPeakMemoryBytes for classic-engine stages ($addFields, $bucketAuto, $graphLookup, $lookup, among others) at executionStats verbosity or higher. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, aggregation explain, explain plan, spill statistics, Aggregation Explain and Spill Statistics ($lookup and $group and memory limits)
- [fact] With executionStats or allPlansExecution, spill-capable stages ($sort, $group, $setWindowFields, $bucketAuto, $graphLookup, and $lookup only under the slot-based engine) report usedDisk, spills, spilledBytes (estimate before compression), spilledRecords and spilledDataStorageSize. MongoDB 8.1 adds $text queries using the TextOr stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: aggregation explain, explain plan, spill statistics, Aggregation Explain and Spill Statistics ($lookup and $group and memory limits)
- [fact] A $lookup stage in executionStats or allPlansExecution explain (since 5.0) reports totalDocsExamined, totalKeysExamined, collectionScans, indexesUsed and executionTimeMillisEstimate, so inner-side collection scans are visible. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: aggregation explain, explain plan, spill statistics, Aggregation Explain and Spill Statistics ($lookup and $group and memory limits)
- [fact] MongoDB 6.0+ can run $lookup in the slot-based engine only if all preceding stages are also SBE-eligible, so the same pipeline may or may not produce $lookup spill metrics depending on engine selection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: aggregation explain, explain plan, spill statistics, Aggregation Explain and Spill Statistics ($lookup and $group and memory limits)
- [statement] Hash-based $lookup (HashLookupStage in SBE) is chosen by heuristics only for small data, so spilling is possible but very unlikely; the regular SBE HashJoinStage did not support spilling. The improvement ticket SERVER-74293 is unresolved with a proposal to close it Won't Do. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-74293 · keywords: aggregation explain, explain plan, spill statistics, Aggregation Explain and Spill Statistics ($lookup and $group and memory limits)
- [fact] Aggregation explain on a multi-shard run reports a splitPipeline with shardsPart (stages executed on each shard) and mergerPart (stages executed once at the merge point), plus a shards section keyed by shard name; a single-shard or unsharded run shows only a flat stages array with no splitPipeline. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-18444 · keywords: aggregation explain, explain plan, sharded explain, Sharded Explain and Split Pipelines (SHARD_MERGE and per-shard stats and merge shard selection)
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, `explain` outputs the following field: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#query-knobs · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, explain plan, explain
- [fact] 8.3.3 (June 9, 2026) added CBR observability: explain output (SERVER-115402), serverStatus metrics (SERVER-120369, under metrics.query.cbr incl. count, choseWinningPlan, numPlans, numPlansFailedCostEstimation, numPlansTiedCostEstimation, samplingMicros) and $queryStats metrics (SERVER-117199); SERVER-118434 made CBR eligible during query planning. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/8.3/ · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, explain plan, Cost-Based Ranker and Multi-Planning Changes (8.3 and 9.0)
- [fact] Both the classic multi-planner and CBR store the chosen plan in the plan cache and reuse it for the same plan cache query shape; explain ignores existing plan cache entries and creates none. A bad plan chosen once can therefore persist for a shape until a DDL event, LRU eviction, restart or manual clear. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.3/core/query-plans/ · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, cost-based ranker, explain plan, Cost-Based Ranker and Multi-Planning Changes (8.3 and 9.0)
- [passage] **Changed in version 8.3** — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/text.md#memory-limits · keywords: MongoDB 8.3, spill statistics
- [passage] - `SHARD_MERGE` for merging results from shards — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#classic-execution-engine · keywords: explain plan, sharded explain, SHARD_MERGE · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] Float that represents the estimated abstract cost units used to execute the cost-based ranker per stage. The cost-based ranker chooses the plan with the lowest top level `costEstimate`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: cost-based ranker, explain plan, costEstimate · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] Float that represents the estimated number of documents or keys produced by the stage of the cost-based ranker. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: cost-based ranker, explain plan · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] A significant difference between the `numKeysEstimate` and the `costEstimate` can indicate issues with the `winningPlan`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: cost-based ranker, explain plan, numKeysEstimate, costEstimate, winningPlan · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [fact] Merge-sort visibility: from 4.2 the merge sort moved into $mergeCursors and vanished from explain's mergerPart (4.0 showed a $sort with mergePresorted:true); SERVER-57383 restored it by showing $mergeCursors at the front of mergerPart, fixed in 5.3.0 (resolved 2022-01-20). The practical-aggregations guide describes the omission as affecting 4.2 to 5.2 only. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-57383 · keywords: explain plan, sharded explain, Sharded Explain and Split Pipelines (SHARD_MERGE and per-shard stats and merge shard selection)
- [statement] The older explain boolean needsPrimaryShardMerger was targeted for replacement by a merger-type field (SERVER-30480, fixed 3.5.12, 2017-08-21); the ticket notes the exact merging shard may be unknown at explain time. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-30480 · keywords: explain plan, sharded explain, Sharded Explain and Split Pipelines (SHARD_MERGE and per-shard stats and merge shard selection)
- [statement] Single-shard targeted aggregations: SERVER-18444 (fixed 3.1.4, 2015) asked that explain state the pipeline ran directly on one shard and name its host; before that such runs showed no shard identity. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-18444 · keywords: explain plan, sharded explain, Sharded Explain and Split Pipelines (SHARD_MERGE and per-shard stats and merge shard selection)
- [fact] MongoDB documents explain output as intended for humans, subject to change between releases, and says split-pipeline optimizations can change; do not hard-code parsers against field layout, and note output differs between classic and slot-based engines. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v7.0/core/aggregation-pipeline-sharded-collections/ · keywords: explain plan, sharded explain, Sharded Explain and Split Pipelines (SHARD_MERGE and per-shard stats and merge shard selection)

- [passage] Pipeline stages that require more than 100 megabytes of memory to execute write temporary files to disk by default. - [passage] For any given query, the MongoDB query planner chooses and caches an efficient query plan given the available indexes. - [passage] If the attempt is unsuccessful, MongoDB applies a set of rules to decide whether the multi-planner should continue or if CBR should evaluate the plans to determine the optimal solution. CBR evaluates each node in a plan based on a cost function and its cardinality estimations. MongoDB selects the plan with the lowest overall cost as the winning plan. Currently, MongoDB only invokes the CBR for a small amount of queries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#query-plan-options · keywords: cost-based ranker

- [fact] SERVER-9507 (the $first optimization) was fixed in 4.1.4 (resolved 2018-09-26). SERVER-37304 extended it to $group expressions using exclusively $last by running the DISTINCT_SCAN in reverse; fixed in 6.3.0-rc0 (resolved 2022-12-08). — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-9507 · keywords: DISTINCT_SCAN, $group $first Loose Index Scan (DISTINCT_SCAN for sort-group-first)
- [statement] Planner conditions (per a MongoDB author's description): a matching index with the right sort order (scan direction may be flipped), and group fields not multikey. If met, the pipeline is rewritten to DISTINCT_SCAN plus a $groupByDistinct. This is a single-author description, not the manual. — https://dev.to/franckpachot/firstlast-per-group-postgresql-distinct-on-and-mongodb-distinctscan-performance-1e9d · keywords: DISTINCT_SCAN, $group $first Loose Index Scan (DISTINCT_SCAN for sort-group-first)
- [statement] Rewrite from $sort+$group($first/$last) to $group with $top/$bottom (dropping the blocking $sort) is only a proposal: SERVER-85213 is Backlog with no fix version (last updated 2025-10-24), split into SERVER-87590 ($first/$last) and SERVER-87591 ($firstN/$lastN). DISTINCT_SCAN with $top/$bottom (SERVER-84347) is closed. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-85213 · keywords: DISTINCT_SCAN, $group $first Loose Index Scan (DISTINCT_SCAN for sort-group-first)
